subject: Audit snapshot fallback plan — temporary KMS carveout + SSO handoff
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@clearhealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit snapshot ask for onboarding pilot

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Dedicated last week. We have one compliance gating ask before we can turn on production traffic for the pilot: ClearHealth needs a way to obtain daily immutable audit snapshots for a 30-day pilot window.

Key constraints we have to meet for our internal auditors:
- Snapshots must include request-level metadata (timestamp, model id, route, token counts) and the K/V cache markers used for deduplication.
- Snapshots need to be delivered to our S3 bucket nightly and kept immutable (read-only) for the duration of the pilot.
- If we cannot use Redwood-managed KMS, we need an exception path where ClearHealth supplies a temporary external key for the snapshot object encryption.

Can you confirm whether that is doable within your Dedicated offering, and if a temporary carveout for customer-supplied keys is possible for this pilot? If not, what fallback options do we have for meeting the auditors?

I attached a short extract of the audit requirements the auditor sent. Procurement is looped on details. Hoping to lock this by EOD Friday so we can keep the onboarding schedule.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Security & Compliance Program Manager
ClearHealth

Attachments: audit_snapshot_requirements.pdf (stub)
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.example
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, grace_oconnor@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot ask for onboarding pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Replying with our current options and suggested short-term fallback.

Options today:
1) Native snapshots + Redwood-managed KMS (fastest): We can produce nightly snapshot bundles of request metadata and KV markers and deliver to an S3 endpoint. Objects will be encrypted with Redwood-managed KMS keys.
2) Customer-supplied key (temporary carveout): We can support an ingest pipeline that accepts client-encrypted blobs (you encrypt locally and push). We do NOT currently support customer-managed KMS keys on snapshot objects in Dedicated out-of-the-box.

Suggested fallback (pilot-friendly):
- We can provide the nightly snapshot export to a Redwood-controlled staging S3, encrypt with our KMS, and then perform a transfer to ClearHealth's S3 where you run a server-side re-encryption job using your key (or we can coordinate a short-lived re-encrypt job executed by ClearHealth). This preserves immutability on arrival.

Immediate asks for us to eval feasibility by EOD Friday:
- Grace: can you confirm whether the re-encrypt transfer model satisfies audit requirements for a 30-day pilot, or whether auditors require the object to be encrypted with customer KMS at creation?
- Karthik: ops question — what will the engineering effort look like to automate nightly export + transfer and to mark objects immutable on your S3? I attached a quick MOP draft to show what we'd automate.

Alex — if procurement needs legal language or an interim attestation, we can provide a scoped statement for the pilot.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-mop.xlsx (stub)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.example
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot ask for onboarding pilot

Thanks, Dylan. Quick security assessment: the auditors care about two things — chain-of-custody (who created the encrypted object) and immutability guarantees once the object is under customer control. Both approaches are workable, but there are nuances: 

- Creation-with-customer-KMS: This is the cleanest from an attestation standpoint — object never exists in untrusted key material. We do not currently have automatic CMK (customer-managed KMS) creation for snapshot exports. Enabling full CMK support will require infra changes and a security review (timeline weeks).

- Transfer-and-re-encrypt (recommended pilot path): If ClearHealth receives objects and immediately re-encrypts them with their KMS under a documented, auditable transfer job (we suggest using an S3 Object Lock + legal-hold pattern on arrival), auditors will accept it provided:
   * Transfer job is automated with signed logs (we can emit a transfer manifest with timestamps and checksums).
   * ClearHealth runs re-encryption within <6 hours of arrival and configures S3 Object Lock Governance retention for the 30-day window.

Action items I need to sign off:
- Confirmation from ClearHealth on S3 Object Lock availability and that they can schedule the re-encrypt job within the 6-hour window.
- Karthik to outline the export automation steps and the manifest fields we will emit (request id, model id, route, timestamp, token counts, KV markers).

If both are green, security will provide a scoped pilot attestation doc (one-page) that procurement/legal can attach. If they cannot support Object Lock, we will need to evaluate a short-lived CMK exception — more friction.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.example, dylan_brooks@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, tessa_morgan@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot ask for onboarding pilot — Plan + owners

Alex / team — thanks for patience. We ran a quick intake and here's the plan we can commit to for the 30-day pilot: 

1) Export cadence & format: nightly bundle (UTC 04:00) containing request-level metadata and KV markers. Manifest includes checksums and a signed transfer token. (Owner: Karthik)
2) Transfer + arrival: Redwood writes snapshot objects to a dedicated staging S3 we control in the same region, emits the transfer manifest, and notifies ClearHealth. ClearHealth runs the re-encrypt job (Owner: ClearHealth) within 6 hours. We recommend S3 Object Lock Governance on arrival.
3) Attestation & evidence: Security will provide the one-page pilot attestation and we will surface the transfer manifests in our ops console for the pilot. (Owner: Grace)
4) Exception request if Object Lock is unavailable: Redwood will provision a scoped, time-boxed CMK exception only if auditors require creation-with-customer-KMS and ClearHealth can provide contractual justification. This requires a security review and will slip beyond the pilot window. (Owner: Marissa)

Next steps / timeline:
- Today: Alex to confirm Object Lock availability and that procurement will approve the re-encrypt job SLA.
- Wed EOD: Karthik to share the manifest spec and an automation checklist (JIRA: SEC-1427).
- Thu: Grace to draft the pilot attestation doc and Redwood legal to prepare a short attestation addendum for procurement.
- Fri: Lock plan or escalate to exception path.

Tessa, can you coordinate the ops console readiness so transfer manifests are visible under the ClearHealth tenant? Karthik, please create SEC-1427 and link the proposed-mop.xlsx we used in the intake.

Alex — if that flow is acceptable we'll mark the onboarding schedule as green; if you need object creation under your KMS at source, call that out explicitly and we'll route for exception review.

Marissa Cole
VP Product, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
